solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Announced permission to go through baptism, for example

indicators.note: what is announced is spoken out, so you go by the sound, not the spelling

blocks.note: a right of passage lets you cross; RITE sounds the same as RIGHT

explanation.surface: Someone declares that you are cleared to pass, perhaps at a christening.
explanation.walkthrough: Only the first word changes: RIGHT and RITE are said the same, while OF PASSAGE is spelt identically in both phrases.
explanation.definitionFit: A rite of passage is a ceremony marking a stage of life, and baptism marks entry into the church.

clue.text: Political questions from priest, very lost for fine answer

blocks.note: a reverend is a member of the clergy
v = very; this V is swapped out
f = fine, as on pencil grades; it replaces the V, giving REFEREND

explanation.surface: A priest has lost his way and is looking for a good answer to some political questions.
explanation.walkthrough: Referenda is the Latin plural of referendum, a vote put to the whole electorate on one question.
explanation.definitionFit: Each referendum puts a single political question to the voters.

clue.text: Person who changes views when advantageous better turned out

definitions.text: Person who changes views when advantageous

blocks.clueFragment: Person who changes views when advantageous
blocks.note: an opportunist who adjusts his sails to whichever political wind is blowing
neater in appearance, the comparative of an adjective meaning tidy

explanation.surface: A political turncoat turns out to be the better dressed man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turned out' looks like a verb of changing sides, echoing the turncoat; here it means dressed, as in well turned out. Trim means neat, so trimmer is neater.
explanation.definitionFit: A trimmer is an old name for an opportunist who adjusts his principles to suit the times.

clue.text: Pretended to be missing, first off: showing good judgment, just the same

indicators.note: the first letter is taken off
the same treatment is given again

blocks.clueFragment: showing good judgment, just the same

explanation.surface: Someone faked being lost, which showed good sense after all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Just the same' reads as 'nevertheless'; it is an instruction to repeat 'first off' on the second word.
explanation.definitionFit: Ostensible means professed or apparent rather than real, as a pretended reason is.

clue.text: Forgo second drink, following assistant

explanation.surface: Someone declines another drink after their assistant has had one.
explanation.walkthrough: The wordplay is read backwards: the assistant comes first in the answer although it is last in the clue.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: turning down a chance you are offered is going without it.

clue.text: Policy, ignoring home, includes covering large watch

blocks.note: in = at home; removed from the front to leave SURANCE
l = large, as on clothing sizes

explanation.surface: An insurance policy that excludes the home still covers large items.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is pure insurance jargon: home, covering, large. 'Watch' is the sense of keeping a close eye on someone.
explanation.definitionFit: Surveillance is close observation of a suspect, keeping watch.

clue.text: Player grabbing character from behind: it gets things moving

blocks.note: tau is a Greek letter, a character; reversed to UAT and put inside ACT…OR

explanation.surface: An actor grabs a stagehand from behind, and that gets the scene moving.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Character' suggests a role for the player; it is a letter of the Greek alphabet.
explanation.definitionFit: An actuator is the part of a machine that turns a signal into movement.

clue.text: Hence hesitant dismissal?

blocks.note: er is the sound of hesitation

explanation.surface: A hesitant boss finally sends someone away.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark admits that 'Go!' is a command of dismissal rather than a dismissal itself.
explanation.definitionFit: A Latin word for therefore, used in English logic to introduce a conclusion.

clue.text: Very much in debt for computer deliveries

blocks.note: to be down is to be out of pocket

explanation.surface: Someone has run up huge debts buying things for their computer.
explanation.walkthrough: The two parts sit in reverse order in the clue: 'Very much' becomes the end of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Downloads are files delivered to your computer over the internet.

clue.text: Part of address of monk with a hot reputation

blocks.note: Dom is the title of a Benedictine monk
to make a name for yourself is to win a reputation

explanation.surface: A monk famous for his fiery reputation makes a speech.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Address' reads as a speech or a postal address; it is a web address, whose domain name is the example.com part.
explanation.definitionFit: The domain name is the part of a web address that names the site.

clue.text: Complain joint is under weight

indicators.note: in a down answer, what is under comes below

blocks.note: a hinge is a joint on a door

explanation.surface: Someone moans that their aching joint is carrying too much weight.
explanation.walkthrough: To whinge is British slang for a persistent, peevish moan.
explanation.definitionFit: Whinge means to complain in a whining way.

clue.text: Some wealth in vintage wine perhaps, but not in vintage cars?

definitions.text: Some wealth in vintage wine perhaps, but not in vintage cars?

blocks.clueFragment: Some wealth in vintage wine perhaps
blocks.note: the surface suggests a collector's cellar; the setter means wealth held in a form that is literally a liquid
old cars are solid and slow to sell, so neither literally nor financially liquid

explanation.surface: A collector weighs up whether to invest in fine wine or classic cars.
explanation.walkthrough: Liquid assets are holdings easily turned into cash; the clue plays on wine being a liquid in the everyday sense too.
explanation.definitionFit: Wine is a liquid you own, and liquid assets are the part of your wealth that can be sold quickly.

clue.text: Creating fear, having little hope on this, with a prayer

definitions.note: the second definition gives the phrase A WING, completing 'on a wing and a prayer'

definitions.text: having little hope on this, with a prayer

blocks.clueFragment: having little hope on this, with a prayer
blocks.note: completes a saying about slim hopes: on ___ and a prayer

explanation.surface: Someone frightening, pinning slim hopes on a prayer.
explanation.walkthrough: The saying 'on a wing and a prayer' comes from a wartime song about a damaged plane limping home; 'this' stands for the missing A WING.
explanation.definitionFit: To awe someone is to fill them with reverent fear, so awing is creating fear.

clue.text: Moves to discredit American maps, poorly covering golf

blocks.note: Golf is G in the phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Badly drawn American maps are spread over a golf course.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is all cartography and golf; nothing in it hints at politics until the definition is read as a noun phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: A smear campaign is a series of moves designed to discredit an opponent.

clue.text: Pass off clenched hand having nothing in it

indicators.note: and the thing it has sits inside it

blocks.note: a fist is a clenched hand
O looks like a zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A conjuror shows a closed fist that turns out to be empty.
explanation.walkthrough: The picture is a magician's trick, which suits the definition: foisting is passing off something false.
explanation.definitionFit: To foist a fake on someone is to pass it off as genuine.

clue.text: Wheeze, returning from exam eg at art school

indicators.note: the letters are read going back, right to left
the answer is taken out of the words that follow

blocks.note: exaM EG AT ART School, read right to left

explanation.surface: A student comes back from an art school exam with a breathless story.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wheeze' suggests a breathless student; in British slang a wheeze is a clever scheme or trick.
explanation.definitionFit: A wheeze is a crafty plan, and a stratagem is a scheme to outwit someone.

clue.text: Seek information from contents of tiny pile of paper

indicators.note: the contents of a word are its inside letters

blocks.note: a quire is a set of 24 or 25 sheets of paper

explanation.surface: Someone digs through a small stack of papers looking for facts.
explanation.walkthrough: QUIRE is an old measure of paper, a twentieth of a ream.
explanation.definitionFit: To inquire is to ask questions, seeking information.

clue.text: What could indicate hour of novelist our realm viciously suppresses

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 8 letters, arranged around MANN

explanation.surface: A writer complains that the country is savagely censoring him.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the hour on a clock face, where XII or IV may mark the time.
explanation.definitionFit: Many clock faces use Roman numerals, so one could indicate the hour.

clue.text: Circus more splendid after installing good place for band

explanation.surface: A circus becomes grander after booking a good spot for the band to play.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Band' suggests musicians under the big top; it is a wedding band, worn on the ring finger.
explanation.definitionFit: A wedding ring, or band, is traditionally worn on the ring finger.

clue.text: Like some walking old way through six counties — cold

blocks.note: Northern Ireland is made up of six counties

explanation.surface: A hiker follows an old path across Northern Ireland in chilly weather.
explanation.walkthrough: Nordic walking uses a pair of poles, like cross-country skiing without the snow.
explanation.definitionFit: Nordic walking is a fitness style using ski-like poles, so the answer describes some walking.

clue.text: After short glance, noticed daughter not occupied at this

explanation.surface: A parent glances over and sees their daughter has nothing to do.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition leans on the idiom: someone with nothing to do is at a loose end, so 'this' stands for the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Being at a loose end means having nothing to occupy you.

clue.text: Reworked and hence improved

indicators.note: the letters are worked over into a new order

explanation.surface: A draft was reworked and so got better.
explanation.walkthrough: 'And hence' reads as a logical link joining two verbs; it is the whole of the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: something enhanced has had its quality raised.

clue.text: No case for illegal trade with a tropical product

indicators.note: the word loses its case, its outer letters

blocks.note: traffic is illegal dealing, as in drug traffic; losing T and C leaves RAFFI

explanation.surface: A lawyer says there is no case against someone smuggling tropical goods.
explanation.walkthrough: 'No case' sounds like a court ruling; it strips the outer letters off TRAFFIC.
explanation.definitionFit: Raffia is fibre from the leaves of a tropical palm, used for weaving and tying.

clue.text: Let a man go who acts without restraint

definitions.note: a relative clause standing for the person who does this

blocks.note: to let go is to free; 'go' completes the phrase

explanation.surface: A prisoner is released and now does as he pleases.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Let go' wraps around 'a man', as in 'let a man go', so the verb splits in the clue but reads as one piece.
explanation.definitionFit: A free agent is someone who can act as they choose, answerable to nobody.

clue.text: Voracious, finally seize certain books I must open

indicators.note: I opens up the letters and goes inside them

blocks.note: NT = New Testament, books of the Bible
as printed; goes inside SURE NT as SUR(I)ENT

explanation.surface: A greedy reader grabs certain books and insists on opening them himself.
explanation.walkthrough: Esurient is a rare, literary word for greedy, from the Latin for being hungry.
explanation.definitionFit: Esurient means hungry or greedy, which is voracious.

clue.text: Spaniard with a Welsh girl — as they say, ladies first

indicators.note: go by the sound of what people say

blocks.note: the ladies is a women's toilet, a loo; written as it is said
Sian is a common Welsh girl's name

explanation.surface: A Spaniard escorts a Welsh girl, politely letting women go first.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ladies first' reads as good manners; it also places the loo before SIAN. In Britain the ladies is the women's toilet.
explanation.definitionFit: An Andalusian comes from Andalusia in southern Spain.

clue.text: Shamed, dig sacred ground

indicators.note: the letters are ground up, crushed into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone was shamed for digging up holy ground.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ground' looks like the noun, land, completing 'sacred ground'; it is the verb, crushed.
explanation.definitionFit: Disgraced means brought into shame.

clue.text: One has stacks to clean when my pieces crumble

explanation.surface: Someone groans at the pile of cleaning they face when their things fall apart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stacks' suggests heaps of work; they are chimney stacks.
explanation.definitionFit: A chimney sweep's job is cleaning chimney stacks.

clue.text: Harsh demand for money in divorce case?

blocks.note: an ex is a former spouse
a legal action is a case in court

explanation.surface: A spouse makes a punishing claim for money during divorce proceedings.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the loose reading: an ex's action is a divorce case, and 'in' only joins the parts.
explanation.definitionFit: An exaction is a harsh or unjust demand, especially for payment.

clue.text: Stress vote for the left?

blocks.note: to dwell on a point at excessive length
a two-word plea to side with Britain's main left-wing party

explanation.surface: A canvasser keeps pressing the case for voting left.
explanation.walkthrough: The Labour Party is Britain's main party of the left, so 'be Labour' is a call to vote for it.
explanation.definitionFit: Overemphasis: you labour a point by going on about it long after it is made.

clue.text: Head off accident? Not careful enough

indicators.note: the head, the first letter, comes off

explanation.surface: A driver tries to prevent a collision but is too careless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Head off' reads as prevent; it means cut the first letter off.
explanation.definitionFit: A rash act is one done without enough care or thought.

clue.text: Avoid female authors, with TLS heartlessly making small changes

blocks.note: to avoid women writers, READ JUST MEN

explanation.surface: A literary reviewer at the TLS shuns women writers and coldly tweaks their copy.
explanation.walkthrough: The TLS is the Times Literary Supplement, a British book review paper. 'Avoid female authors' is a playful phrase for READ JUST MEN.
explanation.definitionFit: Readjustments are slight alterations made to set something right again.

clue.text: Disclaim holding corps, disloyal no longer

definitions.note: 'no longer' marks the answer as an archaic word for disloyal

blocks.note: to recant is to take back what you said
RE = Royal Engineers, an army corps

explanation.surface: A soldier renounces his old regiment and swears he is no longer a traitor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Disloyal no longer' reads as a reformed traitor; 'no longer' says the word is out of use.
explanation.definitionFit: Recreant is an old word for unfaithful or cowardly, a deserter of a cause.

clue.text: Old sheep with one shoulder cut cured

blocks.note: a ram is a male sheep
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A butcher takes an old sheep and cures a cut of its shoulder.
explanation.walkthrough: The sheep invites lamb or mutton; pastrami is spiced, smoked beef.
explanation.definitionFit: Pastrami is a cut of beef, often shoulder or brisket, that has been cured and smoked.

clue.text: Standing quietly, nothing grand here

blocks.note: piano is the musical direction for playing softly

explanation.surface: Someone stands silently in a modest room with nothing impressive in it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nothing grand' reads as humble; it says this piano is not a grand piano.
explanation.definitionFit: An upright piano stands vertically, the alternative to a grand.

clue.text: Irish revolutionary moving left holds news channels beyond salvation

blocks.note: a rebel is a revolutionary; with L moved left it is REBLE
the media carry the news; held as RE(MEDIA)BLE

explanation.surface: An Irish rebel shifts his politics leftwards and captures the newspapers, a hopeless cause.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Moving left' reads as a political shift; it moves the letter L one step to the left.
explanation.definitionFit: Irremediable means impossible to cure or put right.

clue.text: Songs went high up at this rate

blocks.note: 'went' as a euphemism for going to the toilet

explanation.surface: Some tunes soared high at a great pace.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Went' is the coy sense of relieving yourself, as in 'I need to go'.
explanation.definitionFit: Airspeed is the rate at which an aircraft moves through the air, high up.

clue.text: River creature in land legally acquired by temple

blocks.note: a wat is a Buddhist temple in Thailand or Cambodia
terra is the Latin word for land used in legal phrases

explanation.surface: A river animal lives on land a temple bought legally.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Legally' tells you to use the Latin of legal documents, where land is terra.
explanation.definitionFit: The water rat, or water vole, lives on riverbanks, like Ratty in The Wind in the Willows.

clue.text: Nobody has energy to move something inert

indicators.note: the E is moved to a different spot

blocks.note: the E of NONE moves up to second place

explanation.surface: Nobody can be bothered to shift a lump that won't budge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Energy' reads as get-up-and-go; it is the E already in NONE, which is moved.
explanation.definitionFit: Neon is one of the inert or noble gases, which hardly react with anything.

clue.text: Bull in mortuary?

blocks.note: the bull is the bullseye, the exact middle of a target
a mortuary is a centre for the dead

explanation.surface: A bull has somehow ended up in a morgue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bull' looks like the animal; in darts and shooting it is the bullseye.
explanation.definitionFit: The bull is the exact middle of a target, its dead centre.

clue.text: Immunity may be so complex to claim with depression on top

indicators.note: the letters are made complicated, rearranged

explanation.surface: Claiming immunity is complicated if you are feeling low.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Depression' suggests mood; it is a dip in the ground.
explanation.definitionFit: Diplomatic immunity shields envoys from prosecution in the country where they serve.

clue.text: Sailor apparently ready for burial who suddenly jumps up

definitions.note: a relative clause standing for the thing that does this

blocks.note: Jack, or Jack Tar, is a sailor
someone in a coffin looks ready to be buried

explanation.surface: A sailor laid out in his coffin suddenly sits bolt upright.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is a horror film joke: a corpse leaping up, which is exactly what the toy does.
explanation.definitionFit: A jack-in-the-box is a toy figure that springs up out of its box when the lid opens.

clue.text: Noticed his failing, pleasure-seeking

indicators.note: the letters break down and fall into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone spotted a friend's weakness for the good life.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Failing' looks like a noun, a flaw; it is a verb telling you the letters collapse.
explanation.definitionFit: Hedonistic means devoted to the pursuit of pleasure.

clue.text: Church never more pessimistic?

blocks.note: the opposite of 'ever more' is 'ever less', with ever shortened to poetic E'ER

explanation.surface: A gloomy churchgoer declares nothing will ever get better.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Never more' is turned inside out to 'e'er less'; the question mark covers both that twist and the loose definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone cheerless is gloomy, much as a pessimist is.

clue.text: Some underwear poet hasn’t finished wearing

blocks.note: a bra is an item of underwear

explanation.surface: A poet is caught only half dressed, wearing a bit of underwear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wearing' reads as dressed in; it is the sense of wearing away, as sandpaper does.
explanation.definitionFit: An abradant wears surfaces down by rubbing, like an abrasive.

clue.text: Miserable day and hour regularly for holy man

indicators.note: take letters at regular intervals, every other one

explanation.surface: A miserable day and hour pass for a holy man at prayer.
explanation.walkthrough: A saddhu, or sadhu, is a Hindu holy man who has given up worldly life.
explanation.definitionFit: Saddhu is a variant spelling of sadhu, a wandering Hindu ascetic.

clue.text: Gorgeous bachelor leaves crowd in aftermath of a party

indicators.note: the B leaves the word, dropping out

explanation.surface: A handsome single man slips out of the crowd after a party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gorgeous bachelor' reads as one phrase; the bachelor is only the B that goes.
explanation.definitionFit: Adorable means delightful and lovable, and gorgeous can mean just that.

clue.text: Very happy building’s first illuminated by helium

blocks.note: He is the chemical symbol for helium

explanation.surface: A building lit up by helium lamps looks cheerful.
explanation.walkthrough: The science picture of helium lighting hides three quick abbreviations.
explanation.definitionFit: Blithe means carefree and joyful.

clue.text: On application, obtain date

blocks.note: a patent, licence or loan is obtained by applying for it
to take someone out is to go on a date with them

explanation.surface: Someone fills in a form to get a date.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Date' looks like a calendar day; it is the verb, to court someone.
explanation.definitionFit: To take out a loan or policy is to obtain it after applying.

clue.text: One fleeced, put up initially across better city

indicators.note: in a down answer, putting up reads the letters from bottom to top

blocks.note: to cap a story is to better it
LA = Los Angeles; CAP LA reversed gives ALPAC

explanation.surface: A swindled gambler raises a stake on a city bet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fleeced' suggests cheated, but the alpaca is literally shorn of its fleece.
explanation.definitionFit: Alpacas are South American animals kept and sheared for their wool.

clue.text: Long to throttle editor, a nit-picker

blocks.note: to pant for something is to long for it

explanation.surface: A writer wants to strangle the editor who fusses over every detail.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface paints the author's revenge on a fussy editor, and the editor is also the nit-picker it describes.
explanation.definitionFit: A pedant fusses over small details, as a nit-picker does.

clue.text: After second refusal, I cut into staff’s legal rights

blocks.note: a mo is a moment, a second
a pole is a staff, and staff's gives POLE'S

explanation.surface: After a second refusal, someone cuts into the workforce's rights.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Staff' reads as employees; it is a pole, a long stick.
explanation.definitionFit: A monopoly can be an exclusive legal right to trade in something, as a patent grants.

clue.text: Part of minor thoroughfare that is magnetically attractive

definitions.note: a relative clause standing for the direction

indicators.note: the answer is only part of the words that follow

explanation.surface: A little side street has some magnetic charm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Magnetically attractive' reads as charm; it means a compass needle is drawn towards magnetic north.
explanation.definitionFit: A compass needle is pulled towards the magnetic north.

clue.text: Mean bracket I carved as woodworker

indicators.note: the letters are cut up and reshaped

explanation.surface: A carpenter admits he carved a rather poor shelf bracket.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Carved' suits the woodworking picture exactly while quietly telling you to rearrange the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A cabinet-maker is a skilled woodworker who makes fine furniture.

clue.text: Greens joined by a star

explanation.surface: A plate of greens shares the bill with a celebrity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A star' reads as one phrase; the A goes into the answer and the star alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Vega is one of the brightest stars in the northern sky, in the constellation Lyra.

clue.text: Bliss, having vehicle in wild rain

blocks.note: a van is a vehicle; it sits inside the jumbled rain

explanation.surface: Being snug in your camper van during a storm is pure bliss.
explanation.walkthrough: The picture is a cosy van in a downpour; nirvana comes from the Buddhist state of perfect peace.
explanation.definitionFit: Nirvana is a state of perfect happiness, bliss.

clue.text: A certain ploy gaining area for time in the country

blocks.note: the definite article marks a certain one
a gambit is an opening ploy
t = time; swapped out, so GAMBIT becomes GAMBIA

explanation.surface: Someone tries a particular trick to buy land out of town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In the country' reads as rural; 'country' is the definition. The Gambia is a small West African nation.
explanation.definitionFit: The Gambia is a country in West Africa, whose name officially keeps the article.

clue.text: Recurring idea for rejecting English wine

indicators.note: what is rejected is sent back, so the letters are read backwards

explanation.surface: A critic keeps turning down English wine as a matter of principle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rejecting' reads as snobbery about English wine; it sends E PORT back to front.
explanation.definitionFit: A trope is a recurring theme or motif in stories and art.

clue.text: Up to 18, not keen about Henry wearing green

blocks.note: H is the henry, the unit of inductance; COOL around it is CHOOL
sage is a grey-green colour; it is worn outside CHOOL

explanation.surface: A teenager is lukewarm about a boy called Henry dressed in green.
explanation.walkthrough: Henry looks like a person's name; it is H, the physics unit.
explanation.definitionFit: Children under 18 are of school age, when they are expected to be in education.

clue.text: Certifies I ate a chestnut that is bad

indicators.note: the letters have gone bad and come out in a new order

explanation.surface: Someone confirms that they ate a chestnut that had gone off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Chestnut' suggests a stale joke as well as a nut; either way it is just fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: To authenticate a document or object is to certify that it is genuine.
